lead: 9 kilometres of green park crossing Valencia from west to east along the old bed of its river. A masterpiece of urban planning born of a tragedy that became the city’s greatest green treasure.

The Turia Garden runs along the old riverbed for more than nine kilometres free of cars, connecting the Parque de Cabecera and the Bioparc in the west with the City of Arts and Sciences in the east. Designed in 18 sections by different urban planners and landscape architects, each section has its own character: pine woods, sports fields, orange and palm gardens, children’s areas and Valencia’s most iconic skyline in the background.

Access is completely free and the garden never closes. It is the open-air gym, the meeting place and the green lung of the whole city. One of the reasons Valencia was named European Green Capital 2024.

items.kicker: Western end · Nature and African wildlife
items.title: Parque de Cabecera and Bioparc
items.subtitle: Artificial lake · Swan boats · Bioparc · Riverside Wood
items.body: The western start of the Turia Garden is the Parque de Cabecera, designed to recover the river’s historic landscape. It has three main areas: the Colina Mirador — a visual landmark from which to look over the city —, the Riverside Wood that links the land and water environments, and the artificial lake where you can hire swan-shaped boats. Next to the Parque de Cabecera is the Bioparc, one of the best zoos in Europe, where the African savannah, the forests of Madagascar and equatorial Africa are faithfully recreated without visible bars. The stretch was refurbished in 2007.
facts: Colina Mirador, Riverside Wood and artificial lake with boats
One of the best zoos in Europe · African savannah · Paid admission
Metro L1 Nou d’Octubre stop · Av. Pío Baroja

items.title: Central Section · Urban Forest and Sport
items.subtitle: Circuit 5K · Sports fields · Mediterranean pines · Serranos area
items.body: The central sections of the garden combine the “Urban Forest” designed by the Consellería de Agricultura — with thousands of Mediterranean pines that create a true forest inside the city — with the park’s most complete sports area. The Circuit 5K Jardí del Turia, an earth-coloured running track specially designed for runners, runs through these sections. There are also rugby, baseball, athletics and football pitches, multi-sport courts, skateboarding, mini-golf, a climbing wall, pétanque courts and outdoor gym areas. The walk through the Serranos area connects directly with the Serranos Towers and El Carmen district.
facts: Running track exclusively for runners · Earth-coloured · No crossings
Athletics, rugby, baseball, football, skate, mini-golf, pétanque, climbing wall

items.title: Palau de la Música and Nursery Area
items.subtitle: Ricardo Bofill · Orange trees and palms · Cultural area
items.body: The stretch of garden next to the Palau de la Música was designed by the architect Ricardo Bofill with an elegant aesthetic of orange trees, palms and flower beds. The Palau de la Música — built in 1987 by José María García Paredes — has a glass dome that seeks total integration with the garden. On the outdoor esplanade, skates, scooters and children’s games fill the square at weekends. This stretch also connects with the Jardines del Real (Viveros), Valencia’s historic garden with its botanical collection and its great centuries-old ficus trees. Calatrava’s Puente de la Exposición — popularly “la peineta” — stands in this stretch.

items.title: Gulliver Park
items.subtitle: 70 m giant figure · Slides · Ladders · Ropes · Free
items.body: Gulliver Park is one of the best-loved corners of Valencia. Located in section 12 and designed by Rafael Rivera and Manolo Martín, it recreates the moment when Gulliver arrives in Lilliput and is tied down by the Lilliputians — who, in this case, are the visitors. The giant fibreglass figure is 70 metres long and is full of slides, ladders, ramps and ropes that children climb freely. Admission is completely free. The park usually opens from 10:00 to 20:00 (later in summer) and is one of the most photogenic places in Valencia.
facts: 70 metres long · Fibreglass · Slides and ladders built in
About 10:00–20:00 · Later in summer · Occasionally closed for maintenance

items.kicker: Eastern end · Avant-garde architecture by Calatrava
items.title: City of Arts and Sciences
items.subtitle: Oceanogràfic · Museu de les Ciències · Hemisfèric · Palau de les Arts · Umbracle
items.body: The eastern end of the Turia Garden flows into Valencia’s most iconic architectural complex: the City of Arts and Sciences, designed by Santiago Calatrava. The Garden connects seamlessly with the complex’s lakes, where students from Berklee Valencia give free open-air concerts in the series “A Lake of Concerts”. The Umbracle, with its large-format sculptures and Mediterranean garden, is the green link between the park and the buildings. It is the perfect finishing point for the full garden route.
facts: The Turia Garden flows directly into the lakes of the CAC
“A Lake of Concerts” · Berklee Valencia students · All year round

items.kicker: Heritage · From the 15th to the 21st century
items.title: 18 Historic and Modern Bridges
items.subtitle: Puente de la Trinidad (15th c.) · Calatrava · Puente de las Flores
items.body: The Turia Garden is crossed by 18 bridges that offer an involuntary tour through the history of Valencia’s architecture. The oldest is the Puente de la Trinidad, in 15th-century Gothic style. The most photogenic are Santiago Calatrava’s three: the Puente del 9 de Octubre (1989, Calatrava’s first), the Puente de la Exposición or “la peineta” (1995) and the Puente de l’Assut de l’Or or “el jamonero” (2008). The Puente de las Flores, covered in flowering pots all year round, is the most romantic. The Puente de Serranos was recently pedestrianised.
facts: 15th century · Gothic style · The oldest on the route
9 de Octubre (1989), Exposición (1995) and Assut de l’Or (2008)

blocks.title: Tips for exploring the Turia Garden
items: The bike is the best way to cover the 9 km: Valenbisi has stations along the whole route
Gulliver Park is free: arrive first thing in the morning on a weekday to enjoy it without queues
The free Berklee concerts on the CAC lake are especially moving at sunset
For running, the Circuit 5K has an exclusive, signposted earth-coloured track: no bikes or pedestrians
The Puente de las Flores is the most romantic: especially pretty in spring when the geraniums are in bloom
The Gran Feria de Valencia in July fills the garden with rides, concerts and fireworks
